definition: Punitive means intended to punish — describing measures, fines, or actions designed to make a wrongdoer suffer a cost.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word punitive. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know punitive should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The rental contract hides punitive fees that charge triple the daily rate for every hour a car is returned late.
A strict rule demands obedience, but a punitive rule is designed to make violators suffer a real cost.
Draconian is stronger than punitive, describing punishments so extreme they seem cruel for the offense.

Disciplinary describes measures an institution takes against its own members to enforce its rules — a school suspends, an employer writes up. Punitive is broader and harsher in flavor: anything designed to make a wrongdoer suffer a cost, aimed at anyone, member or stranger.

Retributive is the philosopher's word: it justifies a punishment as paying wrongdoing back, balancing the moral books. Punitive is the working adjective courts and contracts actually use — describing fees, damages, and tariffs whose whole design is to make the violator hurt.

Punishing describes anything so harsh it feels like a punishment — a punishing climb, a punishing schedule — with no one intending it. Punitive is strictly about intent: a punitive measure was designed to punish, whatever it ends up feeling like.

Punitive is the adjective for measures intended to punish — punitive damages, punitive tariffs, punitive fines.
It describes the intent behind the measure, not the punishment itself: the specific fine or sentence a wrongdoer actually receives is the penalty, a related but distinct word in this unit.

When the ferry company dumped bilge waste in the bay for the third time, the regulator changed tactics.
The first two fines had been calculated to recover cleanup costs, and the company had quietly paid them as a business expense.
The third fine was punitive: ten times the cleanup cost, set at a level the agency admitted was meant to hurt.
Board members who had shrugged at the earlier penalties called an emergency meeting within a day.
Critics asked whether a penalty should repair or punish; the agency answered that some companies only learn from the second.
